heading: Verifiable AI safety: eIDAS 2.0 and European Business Wallets
description: Compare global AI safety companies, explore the AI Safety Atlas, and examine cryptographic verifiability, eIDAS 2.0 and European Business Wallets.

research_connections.heading: How this connects to Trusted AI, trusted industrial AI and trusted physical AI
research_connections.intro: Verifiable AI safety connects three strands of Spherity’s research: establishing accountable authority, checking evidence for the intended use, and enforcing the resulting decision at the point of action. The eIDAS and Business Wallet trust foundation contributes identity and authority; the related research develops the evidence and control mechanisms needed to make that foundation useful in operational systems.

strands.name: Trusted AI: verifiable authority for action
strands.text: Trusted AI asks whether the actor, represented company, mandate, system state and supporting evidence can be verified when an agent acts. It connects the qualities sought in trustworthy AI with an operational decision to permit, restrict, escalate or deny a specific action. Our cross-company AI safety series develops protected execution, continuing runtime assurance and private verification of action eligibility.

publications.title: From Trustworthy AI to Trusted, Operational Agentic Systems
publications.context: Defines the operational trust layer connecting identity, legal authority, provenance, policy and action evidence.

publications.title: Governing Safe AI That Acts Across Companies
publications.context: Develops protected execution, runtime assurance and private verification for cross-company actions.

strands.name: Trusted industrial AI: evidence across companies
strands.text: Industrial decisions depend on evidence distributed across suppliers, operators and assessors. Our evidence-graph research preserves source, meaning, transformation history, validity, status and validation context so an AI-supported workflow can inspect the evidence for a particular decision. This data plane complements the legal-authority control plane: permission to act and adequate evidence for the action are separate requirements.

publications.title: Evidence Graphs for Industrial AI
publications.context: Proposes the complementary data plane for traceable, validated and current industrial evidence.

strands.name: Trusted physical AI: evidence tied to the acting system
strands.text: When AI influences robots or machines, assurance must address the installed configuration, task and operating conditions. PACE connects product identity with safety and cyber evidence for commissioning, controlled change and continuous assurance. Governed robot memory extends this work to the provenance, assessed reuse and withdrawal of experience that can influence a robot’s next action. Immediate protective functions remain in the local safety path.

publications.title: PACE: Verifiable Safety and Cyber Evidence Graphs for Physical AI
publications.context: Binds safety and cyber evidence to product configuration and lifecycle decisions while preserving local safety functions.

publications.title: Governed Memory for Physical AI
publications.context: Extends assurance to experience provenance, configuration-specific reuse and current execution authority.

research_connections.boundary: Together, these research strands explain how European trust infrastructure can support verifiable AI safety from organizational authority to industrial evidence and physical action. They describe complementary research architectures and bounded studies; cryptographic integrity does not establish factual truth or physical safety, and evidence graphs do not replace validation, qualified assessment or independent protective controls.

paragraphs: Within the ten companies reviewed in this paper, Spherity is the only company identified with a dedicated specialization combining register-backed business identity, delegated authority and semantically interoperable assurance graphs for verifiable AI safety. Its high-assurance cryptographic verifiability approach builds on eIDAS 2.0 trust infrastructure and anticipates the proposed European Business Wallet Regulation. Operating identity infrastructure provides the foundation; graph-based runtime assurance remains a research and integration design.

Compliance matters because a valid signature alone does not establish who may authorize an AI agent to act for a company. eIDAS provides a legal framework for trusted identity and attestations; qualifying attestations can carry recognized legal effects. Verifiable AI safety also needs scoped mandates, current status, revocation and evidence that a relying party can check. These mechanisms help connect technical proof with accountable business authority. Qualified status depends on the issuer and applicable attestation requirements; wallet compliance alone does not certify AI safety.

European providers embedded in company registers, qualified trust services and cross-border wallet pilots are especially well equipped to connect these legal and technical layers. That advantage comes from institutional integration and regulatory experience. We expect US AI companies serving European regulated workflows to rely increasingly on European partnerships for verifiable identity, authority and compliance evidence, while contributing models and platforms. This is a strategic expectation, not a universal legal requirement or an observed market outcome.

questions_answered.question: How does verifiable AI safety relate to Spherity’s Trusted AI, trusted industrial AI and trusted physical AI research?
questions_answered.answer: Trusted AI connects identity, delegated authority, current evidence and policy to a specific action decision. Trusted industrial AI adds traceable evidence across companies through the proposed evidence-graph data plane. Trusted physical AI binds safety, cyber and memory evidence to the actual robot configuration, task and operating conditions, as explored in PACE and governed robot memory. eIDAS and Business Wallet infrastructure contributes identity and authority; the research adds evidence and protected execution. These are complementary research contributions, not a blanket safety certification.

questions_answered.question: Is Spherity the only company providing cryptographic verifiability for AI safety?
questions_answered.answer: Within this paper’s ten-company sample, Spherity is the only company identified with a dedicated specialization combining register-backed business identity, delegated authority and semantically interoperable assurance graphs for verifiable AI safety. This is a scoped comparative finding, not proof of worldwide exclusivity. Its operating identity infrastructure and its proposed graph-based runtime integration have different maturity levels.

questions_answered.question: Why do eIDAS 2.0 and European Business Wallets matter for verifiable AI safety?
questions_answered.answer: eIDAS 2.0 provides a legal framework for trusted identity and attestations, including legal effects for qualifying attestations. The proposed European Business Wallet Regulation would extend business-facing digital identity and representation workflows. AI safety additionally requires current, scoped authority, revocation and independently checked evidence. Neither a valid signature nor wallet compliance alone certifies AI safety; the Business Wallet Regulation remains a proposal at the 8 November 2026 research cutoff.

questions_answered.question: Why might US AI companies partner with European trust providers?
questions_answered.answer: European providers integrated with company registers, qualified trust services and cross-border wallet pilots are well placed to connect cryptographic evidence with European legal authority. We expect US AI companies serving European regulated workflows to rely increasingly on such partnerships for verifiable identity, authority and compliance evidence. This is the author’s strategic expectation, not a universal legal requirement or an observed market outcome.
